WHAT YOU BRING - 6+ years of professional software development experience with a strong focus on consumer-facing web and/or mobile products. - Deep expertise in TypeScript and the React ecosystem, you have opinions about state management, data fetching patterns, and component architecture, and you can articulate the trade-offs. - Production experience with React Native and cross-platform mobile development, including App Store and Google Play release pipelines. - Experience with Next.js — specifically familiarity with App Router, React Server Components, and the client/server boundary decisions that come with them. - Hands-on experience with A/B testing, feature flags, and experimentation frameworks (LaunchDarkly, Optimizely, or similar). - Experience with WebSockets or Server-Sent Events for real-time UI updates. - Strong testing culture Jest, React Testing Library, Playwright or Cypress, and the judgement to know when to use each. - Familiarity with modern build tooling (Vite, Webpack, CI/CD pipelines) and performance profiling. - Experience in fintech, crypto, payments, or other high-trust consumer products where correctness and user confidence matter. - Strong written and verbal English, you can write a clear RFC, give direct feedback in a PR review, and explain a technical trade-off to a non-technical stakeholder. - An active AI-assisted development workflow, Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, or equivalent with the engineering rigour to review and own what gets produced. items.title: Head of Fraud
items.description: ABOUT THE ROLE Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market, and trust in every account, deposit and trade is core to the product. As Head of Fraud, you will own Polymarket's fraud risk end to end: defining the strategy, building preventative and detective controls, and making sure every finding is resolved. Your scope covers first-party fraud (customers abusing the platform themselves) and third-party fraud (bad actors targeting our users and systems, including account takeover). You will hold the bar for what good looks like both commercially and in the eyes of our regulators, and you will move fast. You will partner with and influence Product owners and engineers you don't manage build and ship most fraud controls, so influencing them is critical to success in this role. You'll also work closely with Compliance, Legal, Data, Payments, Customer Support and Security. WHAT YOU'LL OWN Strategy and risk ownership - Own the fraud risk framework and appetite, and set the roadmap to deliver it. - Maintain a living fraud risk assessment and typology library across onboarding, funding, trading and withdrawals. - Report fraud exposure, losses, control performance and emerging threats to senior leadership and governance forums. Preventative and detective controls - Partner with Product and Engineering to assess fraud risk before new products, payment methods, promotions, and material feature changes launch. - Define and implement controls that stop fraud before it happens: identity and device signals, step-up authentication, velocity and limit rules, and payment and withdrawal checks. - Build detective controls that surface fraud fast: monitoring rules, ML and AI models, anomaly detection, alerting and case management. - Tune controls continuously against loss rates, false positives and customer friction. Fraud types in scope - First-party fraud: chargeback and friendly fraud, promotion and referral abuse, ACH fraud, multi-accounting, and identity misrepresentation by genuine customers. - Third-party fraud: account takeover, synthetic and stolen identities, stolen payment methods, phishing, social engineering, scams, and organized fraud rings. You will spend most of your time in the systems and the data, deep-diving into problems: connecting HRIS, ATS, payroll, identity, and finance tools, standing up the data layer behind our people metrics, and shipping automations that remove manual work from the People team. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning. About the role We’re looking for a Designer to create thoughtful, high-quality work across consumer campaigns and brand identity. You’ll contribute original ideas and turn creative direction into finished design across campaigns, digital experiences, social content, presentations, and brand materials. This is a hands-on maker role for someone who enjoys moving between concept development and detailed execution. You’ll work closely with creative leads, writers, marketers, and producers, bringing strong visual craft and an active interest in using AI tools to explore and develop creative work. We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always. We have expanded from voice into three main platforms: - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale. - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages. - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models. Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. HOW WE WORK - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy. - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you. - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations. - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models. - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location. WHAT WE OFFER - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities. - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend. - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose. - Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend. ABOUT THE ROLE We are seeking an experienced Commercial Counsel to join our Legal Team in Brazil. In this role, you will support complex commercial transactions with a primary focus on Brazil and support for other LATAM countries, including SaaS, licensing, and strategic partnerships, while helping the company navigate diverse legal and regulatory frameworks in the rapidly evolving field of artificial intelligence. You will work closely with global colleagues to provide practical, business-oriented advice that enables growth while managing risk across multiple jurisdictions. items.title: Staff Site Reliability Engineer - Dev Platform
items.location_text: Brazil, Peru, Colombia, Argentina, Mexico, Chile
items.description: BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system. THE TEAM Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients. Kraken's engineers build a lot of software. Developer Platform AI builds the AI systems they use to do it: agents that write and review code, simple access to the best models in the tools they already use, and the infrastructure that connects AI to our internal systems. This is a small team with a lot of reach. The tools you ship will change how engineers across Kraken work every day, and you'll see that happen directly. The work spans agent platforms, code review, LLM routing and cost controls, MCP integrations with tools like Slack, Jira and GitLab, and the security and observability that make all of it safe to run. If you want to work on applied AI with real users from day one, this is that job. THE OPPORTUNITY - LLM traffic doesn't behave like normal API traffic. Requests are long-running, streaming and expensive. One prompt can cost a few cents or a few dollars. One team's burst can burn another team's budget. Providers change their rate limits, failure modes and pricing without warning. Running this well is a problem few companies have solved, and it's the job. - Own the reliability of the platform engineers depend on: the AI Gateway, the agent runtime and the connections to internal tools. Set the SLOs, own the error budgets and decide what happens when they're spent. - Design resilience across model providers: routing, failover, retries, rate limiting and graceful degradation when a provider is slow, throttling or down. - Make LLM traffic legible. Build observability that shows latency, errors, token usage and cost by team, model and use case, so engineers can see what their workloads cost and where they're spending their time waiting. - Treat capacity and cost as one problem. Routing decisions affect both latency and spend, and you'll own the tradeoff directly. - Work with Security, Finance and AI governance to put access controls, budgets, audit logging and data handling into the platform, not into a spreadsheet next to it. - Lead incident response and blameless post-incident reviews. Turn what breaks into fixes that stay fixed. - Automate operations with infrastructure as code, safe deployments and progressive rollouts, so the platform gets more reliable as it grows rather than more fragile. - Mentor engineers and raise the operating standard across the team. items.title: Lead Data Engineer
items.description: We’re looking for an Lead Data Engineer to join the Paid Media Insights team within Better Collective. The Domanin Paid media is where the data has to pay off. We spend real money across dozens of ad networks every day. Which campaigns scale, which creatives get cut and which markets get budget comes out of this team’s models. Ad platform spend and delivery, affiliate and operator revenue and CRM, stitched into one user-level view of what a click was worth. That model exists and it works. The most demanding domain on our platform: the most sources, the fastest schema churn, the shortest patience for a late table. We want the engineer who owns it. Where this role sits A central platform team sets the how. You set the what. A central team owns the platform - MotherDuck, dbt, Dagster, DLT, the infrastructure. Paid Media Insights is a spoke in that hub and spoke organisation, building on it. The split is deliberate: the platform team decides how data is produced, you decide what paid media produces and own everything we run. No new stack to build, and no year lost to plumbing a central team should solve once. Be a demanding customer: when a golden path does not fit paid media, push for it to change rather than quietly building around it. You report to the Senior Head of Paid Media Insights and work across Paid Media, with the Campaign, Commercial, CRM and platform teams. What you will own Every data job in paid media. All of it. Freshness, cost, reliability, alerting, and the 07:30 incident before the spend review. A paid media model that is wrong or late is yours, not the platform team’s - that accountability is the core of the role. The end-to-end user-level model. Ad platform spend and delivery, affiliate and operator revenue and CRM, joined into one view the business trusts enough to move budget on. Ingestion of paid media sources on the platform’s framework: which sources, which schemas, and what happens when a network changes its API unannounced. The domain’s models, from staging to the marts analysts query, plus the semantic meaning on top. Nobody at the centre can define a qualified signup in paid media. You can. Reverse ETL into the ad platforms, so conversion data lands where it changes bidding. The handover, taking over the paid media jobs the central team still runs for us. What you will lead A group of engineers, and the standard they build to Technical lead for the data engineers in Paid Media Insights: setting the standard for how this domain builds, reviewing, unblocking, and growing them by giving away the interesting problems. Shaping the domain’s roadmap with the Senior Head of Paid Media Insights, the analysts and the business teams. Representing paid media in platform conversations, including how we support machine learning and data science. Hands-on technical leadership, not a step away from building. You will be in the code. What we’re looking for More than a stack match, we are looking for a particular way of working. You take ownership, and it shows up in the boring parts. You want the pager as well as the model, and would rather own a domain end to end than hand off the consequences. You break complex systems into simple parts. Attribution windows, late conversions, identity across platforms, dozens of disagreeing source APIs - you hold that and still hand the business something it can reason about. You raise the people around you. Colleagues come to you for technical advice. You review generously, give feedback that lands, and would rather the whole team understand the pipeline than be the only one who does. You work well with a platform team. Strong opinions about standards, still happy to work inside someone else’s. You know a constraint worth fighting from a preference worth dropping. You are already past prompting. AI is part of how you engineer, and you have a view on what a data domain needs to be for agents to be useful on top of it: documented, standardised, semantically clear. You are close to the business. You will sit with the marketers and analysts spending budget on what you build, and can talk data with people who do not think in tables. You are technically deep where it counts. Production pipelines in SQL and Python, dbt and Dagster, cloud data warehousing, and a real feel for performance, cost and reliability at scale. Paid media or attribution experience is a bonus. Our Stack What you will build on MotherDuck / DuckDB · dbt · Dagster · DLT · Python · SQL · AWS · reverse ETL and semantic layer tooling We do not expect you to have worked with all of these. If you have built production pipelines on Snowflake, BigQuery or Redshift and you are curious about where we are going, that transfers. Benefits Private health insurance Sick leave 100% paid Canteen with free meals and drinks Flexible working hours Additional vacation days after two years in the company We also provide up-to date equipment, entertainment facilities in a modern office right in the city center and more. Application Deadline We look forward to hearing from you and accept applications until 28th November. Please submit your CV and cover letter in PDF; only applications submitted in English will be considered. Expected start date: as soon as possible.
